theory.intro: A constant function is a horizontal line, so its gradient is $0$ everywhere. A linear function $f(x)=mx+c$ has the same gradient $m$ at every point, so its derivative is $m$.
facts: Rewrite a linear function as $mx+c$ first; for $f(x)=\dfrac{ax+b}{d}$, where $a$, $b$ and $d$ are constants and $d\neq0$, the derivative is $\dfrac{a}{d}$.
The tangent to a straight line at any point is the line itself, so the instantaneous rate of change is $m$ everywhere.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The function is constant, so its graph is horizontal with gradient $0$ everywhere.
$f'(x)=0$

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the derivative of each function.
(a) $f(x)=9-4x$
(b) $y=x$
(c) $g(x)=px+q$, where $p$ and $q$ are constants.
workedExamples.solution_text:
A linear function's derivative is its gradient, the coefficient of $x$.
(a) $f'(x)=-4$
(b) $y'=1$
(c) $g'(x)=p$

Rewrite the function to identify its gradient.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=-\dfrac{5}{6}x+\dfrac{4}{3}\\f'(x)&=-\dfrac{5}{6}\end{align*}$

Expand to identify the coefficient of $x$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=15-10x\\f'(x)&=-10\end{align*}$

Expand and simplify to identify the gradient.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\dfrac{28}{3}-\dfrac{36x}{24}\\&=\dfrac{28}{3}-\dfrac{3}{2}x\\f'(x)&=-\dfrac{3}{2}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A bee flies straight from its hive to a flower $120$ m away in $15$ seconds at a constant speed. Find its speed.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Speed}&=\text{distance}\div\text{time}\\&=120\div15\\&=8\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$
This is the constant gradient of its distance–time graph.

Use the points $(0,30)$ and $(6,6)$.
$\begin{align*}m&=\dfrac{6-30}{6-0}\\&=\dfrac{-24}{6}\\&=-4\end{align*}$
The rate of change is $-4\text{ m/s}^2$.
The vertical intercept is $30$, so $v(t)=-4t+30$.

foundation.question_text: Find the derivative $f'(x)$ for the constant function $f(x)=8$.
What is the gradient of the graph $y=6$ at $x=10$?
foundation.solution_text:
The graph $y=6$ is a horizontal line with gradient $0$ everywhere.
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$

development.question_text: Find $f'(x)$ for $f(x)=ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
A bee flies straight from its hive to a flower $150$ m away in $30$ seconds at a constant speed. What is its speed?

mastery.solution_text:
Gradient $m=\dfrac{1-13}{6-0}$
$=\dfrac{-12}{6}$
$=-2$
The rate of change is $-2\text{ m/s}^2$.
The graph has vertical intercept $13$, so $v(t)=-2t+13$.

$f(x)=\dfrac{(a+5)(a-2)}{a-2}=a+5$
Since $a$ is a constant, $f(x)$ is a constant function.
$f'(x)=0$
